name: What is the difference between a patio cover and a covered deck?

mainEntity.name: What is the difference between a patio cover and a covered deck?

acceptedAnswer.text: A patio cover typically refers to a roof structure built over a ground-level patio, which is usually made of concrete, pavers, or stone. A covered deck, conversely, is a roof structure built over a deck, which is an elevated wooden or composite platform. The primary difference lies in the base structure: a patio is at ground level, while a deck is elevated. A practical tradeoff is the installation complexity; covered decks often require more complex framing and foundation work due to their elevation compared to ground-level patio covers.
acceptedAnswer.description: A patio cover is a roof over a ground-level patio, while a covered deck is a roof over an elevated deck, differing mainly by their base structure.
